WITH invoice_orders AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    o.order_id,
    c.gender
  FROM Invoices i
  INNER JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  INNER JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
),
gender_counts AS (
  SELECT
    gender,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) as order_count
  FROM invoice_orders
  GROUP BY gender
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(order_count) as total FROM gender_counts
),
gender_shares AS (
  SELECT
    gc.gender,
    gc.order_count,
    CAST(gc.order_count AS DECIMAL(38,20)) / CAST(tc.total AS DECIMAL(38,20)) as share
  FROM gender_counts gc
  CROSS JOIN total_count tc
),
average_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM gender_shares
)
SELECT
  gs.gender,
  gs.order_count,
  gs.share,
  gs.share - a.avg_share as difference
FROM gender_shares gs
CROSS JOIN average_share a
WHERE gs.share > a.avg_share
ORDER BY gs.gender;

assumptions.assumption: NULL gender values (if any exist in the Customers table) are treated as a distinct gender category and included in the counting, share calculation, and averaging

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude customers with NULL gender values from the analysis, counting orders only for customers with non-NULL genders
